content2.content: While Flutter provides a rich set of widgets and packages, sometimes you need to access platform-specific APIs that aren't available in the Flutter ecosystem. This section explains how to use Platform Channels to write native code for Android and iOS and call it from your Flutter app.

content4.content: Flutter uses a flexible system called Platform Channels to send messages between Dart and the native platform (Android/iOS). The `MethodChannel` is the most common way to invoke a method on the native side and get a result back.

content6.content: Flutter App (Client) <--> MethodChannel <--> iOS Host (AppDelegate.swift) / Android Host (MainActivity.kt)

content9.content: In your Flutter code, you define a `MethodChannel` with a unique name and invoke methods on it.

content13.content: On the Android side, you listen for method calls in your `MainActivity`.

content17.content: On the iOS side, you handle method calls in your `AppDelegate`.

content21.content: Platform-specific integrations allow you to leverage the full power of the underlying OS. By establishing a `MethodChannel`, you can seamlessly call native code from Dart, enabling you to use any native API or library within your Flutter application.
